built.summary:
Stream T is done: all five findings are fixed. Manager-PIN guessing is now limited in one place. verifyManagerPin (backend/src/modules/auth/managerPin.ts) counts every PIN that is sent, before comparing it, using the new backend/src/lib/managerPinLimit.ts. The limit is 5 attempts per 15 minutes per actor and 5 per order, after which the answer is 429 MANAGER_PIN_LOCKED with details.retryAfterSec. The counter lives on redisFast, with a 750 ms timeout. Every attempt is also counted in process memory and the higher count wins, so neither a Redis outage nor a slow Redis call can double the budget. Each wrong PIN writes an audit row 'manager_pin.failed' with the actor, order and company. The attempt that fills a bucket raises one high-severity flag for the company. A correct PIN resets the actor's count. If the caller passes no actor (trustops petty cash), the actor comes from the request's signed-in user (rlsContext). Every caller now goes through managerPin.ts: discount and price override gates, the line void and order cancel (via requireManagerApproval), refunds and cancelled-ticket refunds (via ensureCapOrManagerOverride), comps, staff meals, till pay-outs and trustops petty cash. PIN length rules are unchanged (4–8 digits, owner decision).

Discounts: a PIN that was sent but is wrong, or belongs to another company, now gets 403 INVALID_MANAGER_PIN. With no PIN at all the answer is still DISCOUNT_OVER_CAP. The discount and price-override alerts are now raised after the order exists and carry its id. Only the discount kind changed; price overrides keep 'high_value_void' until a proper kind is added.

Waste: a line voided after the kitchen fired it is now booked as waste in the void's own transaction (new backend/src/modules/inventory/voidWaste.ts). It only books what the order's depletion actually took for that line. It writes one WasteLog per ingredient (reason 'void_after_fire', moving-average cost, approver recorded). It posts ONE balanced entry, Dr 5040 / Cr 1210, in the ORDER's company, keyed 'pos.void_waste:<orderItemId>' so it cannot post twice. The wasted quantity is also taken off the depletion row's `taken`, so cancelling the order later does not put cooked food back on the shelf. If the period is closed or the ledger refuses the entry, the void still goes through, the waste log stays, and a 'posting_failed' flag goes to the company.

Ring-up: createPosOrder now returns payments { id, method, amountCents, status } and items with their modifiers, on both the new-order and the idempotent-replay paths.

Huge amounts: tender amounts too big for the database column now get 422 AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE instead of a 500. The guard (assertAmountsFit, limit 2,147,483,647 paisa) is in processPayment (amountCents, tenderedCents, tipCents and their sum), settlePayment, compOrder, refundOrder and recordCashMovement.

items.note: Implemented in managerPin.ts and the new lib/managerPinLimit.ts. Attempts are claimed before bcrypt runs, using an atomic Redis Lua INCR+EXPIRE plus an in-memory floor. A parallel burst of 20 guesses gets at most 5 comparisons; the test also covers Redis being disconnected. The flag uses the existing kind 'self_approval' because lib/exceptions.ts has no 'manager_pin_failed' kind; metadata.realKind='manager_pin_failed'. A PIN-less request is not an attempt. A locked request makes no comparison, so it learns nothing. A cashier who is locked out can still have a manager sign in and do the override. PIN length rules are unchanged (owner decision).

Over-cap discount and price override: a wrong or other-company PIN that was sent now gets 403 INVALID_MANAGER_PIN; no PIN still gets DISCOUNT_OVER_CAP / PRICE_OVERRIDE_BLOCKED. The discount flag now uses kind 'comp_above_threshold' (the closest existing kind; metadata.realKind='discount_above_cap'). Both the discount and price-override flags are raised after the order is created, with entityType 'Order' and entityId set to the order id, and only when this request actually created the order. Price overrides still use 'high_value_void' until a kind exists.

New inventory/voidWaste.ts is called from voidOrderItem inside the void's transaction when the line had already been fired. Per ingredient it writes a WasteLog (void_after_fire, unitCost × qty, approver and recorder set). It posts one entry, Dr 5040 / Cr 1210, in the order's company via postJournalEntry({tx}), keyed pos.void_waste:<orderItemId> and checked against period locks. A PERIOD_LOCKED or other AppError from the ledger is caught (it fails before any write, so the transaction stays usable), and a 'posting_failed' flag is raised after commit. The quantity is moved from the depletion row's `taken` into `voidWasted`, so a later cancel does not restore it. COGS already skips voided lines, so nothing is counted twice. The void response gains stockWasted (quantities only, no cost) and the audit metadata records the waste.

Backend half only: RING_UP_INCLUDE = items with modifiers plus payments { id, method, amountCents, status } on both return paths. Tested: a fresh ring-up and its replay both return payments: []. The frontend half (making paidCentsOf tolerate a missing payments array) is listed under needsOtherFiles.

assertAmountsFit returns 422 AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE for any amount above 2,147,483,647, the most a money column (INT4) holds, checked in the payment service functions. Tested through POST /pos/payments with a huge tenderedCents, amountCents and tipCents; no payment row is written.

review.title: A correct PIN clears the sender's whole attempt count, so anyone who knows one valid approver PIN can guess other PINs (the CEO's included) without limit and without any flag
review.scenario:
Reproduced on DB servd_test_rf_t_rv with Redis 6390/12, using a scratch test that was then deleted. pinAttemptSucceeded() (managerPinLimit.ts:194-197) calls clearOne() on the actor bucket. Over-cap discounts (pos/service.ts:207) send no orderId, so the actor bucket is the only limit there.
(a) A foh_management user rings up a Nihari with a 60% discount. That is over managerDiscountCap, so the PIN must belong to an admin. They send 4 guesses, then their OWN PIN. Their own PIN matches, which resets the bucket, and the request still ends in 403 DISCOUNT_OVER_MANAGER_CAP, so nothing is created. Over 4 cycles: 16 x INVALID_MANAGER_PIN, zero MANAGER_PIN_LOCKED, zero exception flags. Repeat until the admin's PIN matches (about 2,000 cycles for a 4-digit PIN; minutes at till speed).
(b) A cashier who knows one manager's PIN (shoulder-surfed or shared) does the same with a 20% discount: 4 guesses, then the known PIN (the order is created and the count resets). 12 wrong guesses, never locked, never flagged. That cashier can then find another manager's PIN and put approvals in that manager's name.
The same reset works on voids and refunds by using a fresh ring-up each time, because the order bucket is per order.
So FOH-R2-01's claim of 5 per 15 minutes per actor does not hold for any sender who holds one valid PIN, which is exactly the insider the finding is about. The PIN-change route (auth/routes.ts ~1229) avoids this on purpose ('release, not clear, so a burst that contains one right answer cannot wipe the others' strikes'). This limiter does the opposite.
review.fix: In pinAttemptSucceeded, release only the successful attempt's own slot on the actor bucket (releaseOne(MANAGER_PIN_ACTOR_LIMIT, keys.actor)), as is already done for the order bucket. Do not clear the bucket. Wrong guesses then still count for the whole 15-minute window, and an honest cashier who mistypes twice and then succeeds keeps 3 spare attempts. Add a regression test with the cycle 4 wrong, then the own or known PIN, then wrong: the 6th wrong attempt must get 429 MANAGER_PIN_LOCKED and raise the flag. Run it once as a manager on a discount over managerDiscountCap and once as a cashier on a discount over cashierDiscountPctCap.

review.title: A locked order uses up the actor slots of honest staff who send the CORRECT PIN, and can lock them out on every order
review.scenario: claimPinAttempt (lines 181-191) claims the actor bucket first and then the order bucket. When the order bucket is full it throws 429 and does not give the actor's slot back ('The actor's slot is not given back: the attempt was made'). But no comparison was made, so nothing was attempted. Example: cashier 1 sends 5 wrong PINs on table 7's order, which locks that order. Cashier 2 then has the manager type the right PIN on table 7 to void a line. Each try gets 429, and each 429 costs cashier 2 an actor slot. After 5 tries cashier 2 is locked out of PIN approvals on every order for 15 minutes, without ever having sent a wrong PIN. No flag names cashier 2, and the audit trail shows no failures for them.
review.fix: In claimPinAttempt, when the order bucket rejects, call releaseOne(MANAGER_PIN_ACTOR_LIMIT, keys.actor) before throwing. That request made no comparison, so the sender should not be charged. An alternative is to check (peek) the order bucket before claiming the actor slot. Add a two-cashier test: cashier 1 locks order X; cashier 2 makes 5 tries with the correct PIN on X and gets 429; cashier 2 can still void on order Y with the correct PIN.

fix.summary:
I fixed both reviewer findings in backend/src/lib/managerPinLimit.ts. The new tests fail on the old code and pass on the fixed code. The touched suites pass and tsc is clean.

T-RV-01 (fixed): a correct PIN used to wipe the sender's whole count. Now `pinAttemptSucceeded` gives back only the slot that attempt took, on the sender and on the order (`releaseOne`, no longer `clearOne`). This is the same "release, not clear" rule the PIN-change route already uses. Someone who knows one valid PIN can no longer reset their wrong guesses every 4 tries. An honest cashier who mistypes twice and then gets it right keeps 3 spare attempts.

T-RV-02 (fixed): when the order's limit is full, `claimPinAttempt` now gives the sender's slot back before returning 429. No PIN was compared, so the sender is not charged. An honest cashier retrying the right PIN on someone else's locked ticket no longer locks themselves out of every order.

I also updated the comments in managerPin.ts and the limiter's header so they no longer say a correct PIN clears the count.

One behaviour to know: the exception flag is raised on the 5th wrong PIN in the window, and the 6th attempt gets 429. The reviewer's wording put the flag on the 6th. The tests follow the code.

items.note: In managerPinLimit.ts, pinAttemptSucceeded now gives back only that attempt's own slot (sender and order) and never clears either count. Tests: as a foh_management user on a 60% discount (over managerDiscountCap): 4 wrong, then their own PIN (403 DISCOUNT_OVER_MANAGER_CAP), then the 5th wrong is INVALID_MANAGER_PIN and raises the flag, and the 6th is 429 MANAGER_PIN_LOCKED. Same cycle as a cashier on a 20% discount (over cashierDiscountPctCap) using a known manager PIN, which creates the order: 5th wrong flags, 6th is 429, nothing in company B. Same cycle on voids with a fresh ring-up each time. The old test 'a correct PIN clears the cashier's count' encoded the defect; it is replaced by 'two mistypes then the right PIN leaves 3 spare'.

In claimPinAttempt, the sender's slot is given back (releaseOne on the sender's count) when the order's limit is full, before the 429. Two-cashier test: cashier 1 locks order X with 5 wrong PINs. Cashier 2 tries the correct PIN 6 times on X and gets 429 each time, and X stays unvoided. Cashier 2 then voids on Y with the correct PIN (200), has no failure audits and no flag, and still gets 403 (not 429) on 4 wrong PINs on a fresh order.

fix.tests: On servd_test_rf_t with Redis 6390/2, tests/resimTill.test.ts passes 20/20. The 4 new tests and the rewritten one all fail when the old clearOne / no-release behaviour is temporarily put back; the fix was restored afterwards. The other suites that use manager PINs all pass, 234/234 across 10 files: auditTillMoney, managerVoids, fiscalTill, auditMoneyFollowups, auditAuthPeople, accessControl, sepTrustops, booksReconcile, resimOnline, resimTill. The 'injected claim failure' Prisma errors in that output are expected output from one of those suites. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` in backend reports no errors.
fix.prodNotes: The limiter now only gives back slots and never clears them on success. Wrong manager PINs therefore count for the whole 15-minute window, whatever correct PINs happen in between. Staff who mistype often across several overrides inside 15 minutes can hit the lock sooner than under the old (exploitable) behaviour. When that happens, a manager signs in and does the override themselves.

review.title: PATCH /concepts/:id now uses scope 'create' (active company only): multi-company CEO, management and marketing get 404 saving a brand that the Brand Editor lists in All-companies view
review.scenario: Reproduced on servd_test_rf_u_rv with a temporary test (since removed). Users admin, management and marketing each have User.tenantId = A and a TenantMember row for B. Each calls GET /concepts?view=brand&includeInactive=1 with x-servd-portfolio: 1, and the result includes B's brand. Each then calls PATCH /concepts/<B brand> {description:'x'}. Results: admin 404 'Concept not found in your active company', management 404 (same message), marketing 404 'Concept ... not found'. At HEAD the management PATCH filtered on req.staffUser.tenantFilter, which the auth middleware widens to every member company on any non-GET request, so this save returned 200. That makes it a regression for the CEO and head-office managers. The admin client also sends no x-servd-active-tenant header on PATCH: frontend/admin/src/lib/api.ts isPortfolioGuarded guards POST only, and its comment says 'PATCH ... the backend derives the tenant from the row itself — every brand-edit save would pop the modal'. So no client-side company pick fixes this. CLAUDE.md: 'write = editing an existing row → every company the operator belongs to; create = binding a new row'. Editing a brand is 'write'. The marketing tier has the same mismatch: it lists brands with scope 'read' (portfolio-expanded) and saves with 'create'. The builder's prodNotes present the change as 'a staffer with no active company now gets 404', which hides this effect on multi-company operators.
review.fix: In both PATCH branches (marketing allow-list and management full schema) look up the owned row with `scopeTenantWhere(req, 'write')` instead of `'create'`. An empty scope still denies, because memberTenantIds is empty for a staffer with no company, giving `{ tenantId: { in: [] } }`. Foreign rows still 404. Keep stamping the audit with owned.tenantId. Add a two-company test: a user with tenantId A and a membership in B can PATCH B's brand, and a user who is not a member of B gets 404.

Management then saves the brand form (the full PATCH always resends logoUrl) and gets 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. updateConceptSchema has `logoUrl: z.string().url()`, while brandMarketingSchema uses brandArtworkUrlSchema, which accepts root-relative paths. Management cannot save any change to that brand (tax, contact, status) until someone clears the logo.
review.fix: Use one rule for logoUrl in both schemas. Either change updateConceptSchema.logoUrl to the same `brandArtworkUrl` rule already used for wordmarkUrl and mascotUrl (http(s) or root-relative, '' clears), or make the marketing schema's logoUrl `z.string().url()`. The first matches what the uploader actually returns.

I confirmed both reviewer findings and fixed them in backend/src/modules/concepts/routes.ts. Regression tests are in backend/tests/resimUi.test.ts. I rejected neither finding.

RV-U-01: both PATCH /concepts/:id branches (the marketing allow-list and management's full schema) now look up the row with scopeTenantWhere(req, 'write'), not 'create'. Editing an existing brand is a write, so it covers every company the operator belongs to (User.tenantId plus TenantMember rows). That matches CLAUDE.md and how the code behaved at HEAD. Brands of companies the operator doesn't belong to still return 404. A staffer with no company still matches nothing, because memberTenantIds is empty and the filter becomes { tenantId: { in: [] } }. The audit is still stamped with the brand's own company (owned.tenantId). The 404 message now says 'Concept not found in your companies', and the comments that said "active company only" are updated.

RV-U-02: createConceptSchema.logoUrl now uses the same brandArtworkUrl rule as wordmarkUrl and mascotUrl, and updateConceptSchema derives from it. That rule accepts http(s) URLs or root-relative paths, '' clears the field, and javascript: and data: URLs are still refused. Both the marketing tier and management's full PATCH now follow the same logoUrl rule. In the full PATCH, a request without logoUrl leaves the stored logo unchanged, because .partial() skips the transform.

items.note: Both PATCH branches now use scopeTenantWhere(req,'write'). New two-company test: admin, management and marketing users with tenantId A plus a TenantMember row for B list B's brand in portfolio view and PATCH it (200). The row stays in B and the audit is stamped B. Users who are only in company A get 404 and nothing is written. Users with no company (management and marketing) get 404.

The full schema's logoUrl now uses the shared brandArtworkUrl rule. Test: marketing saves '/marketing/logo.png'; management's full save that resends it returns 200. javascript: and data: return 400; '' clears the logo; leaving logoUrl out keeps it.

fix.tests: These ran against servd_test_rf_u with Redis 6390/9: tests/resimUi.test.ts (33, including 3 new), storefrontQuickfix (16), auditTillUi (8), brandReconcile (18) and wave3Gates. That is 94/94 passing across 5 files. Backend `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` is clean. No frontend files changed.
fix.prodNotes: This corrects my earlier prodNotes, which said only "a staffer with no company now gets 404". Brand edits (PATCH /concepts/:id) now land in any company the operator belongs to, as at HEAD for management. A multi-company CEO, management or marketing user can save a brand the Brand Editor shows in All-companies view. Brands of companies they don't belong to are still 404, and a staffer with no company is still denied. The audit carries the brand's own company. Brand logo URLs may now be root-relative paths (what the uploader returns when R2_PUBLIC_URL is unset), on create as well as update.
